extracted.intended_audience: researchers planning, conducting, reporting, peer-reviewing, or editing in vivo (animal) experiments; journal editors and reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for what to include when planning and reporting in vivo animal experiments to ensure transparent, rigorous, and reproducible reporting. Covers a prioritized Essential 10 minimum reporting items plus a Recommended Set of contextual items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Design
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items — core information about the overall study design that must be included in any manuscript describing animal research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Essential 10 are the basic minimum items that must be reported so readers and reviewers can assess reliability. Each ARRIVE item has detailed explanations and examples in the Explanation and Elaboration document (PLOS Biology doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.3000411).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items — information about the sample size used in the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sample size determinations and rationale; see the Explanation and Elaboration for examples and guidance. Essential 10 items are required minimum reporting elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items — clear statement of criteria used to include or exclude animals or data from the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe prespecified inclusion/exclusion criteria and any exclusions performed; consult the detailed explanations and example reporting in the E&E document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items — information on whether and how animals/experimental units were allocated randomly to groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report methods of randomisation and sequence generation; see ARRIVE E&E for examples and rationale to minimise bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding/Masking
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items — whether and how blinding was used during allocation, conduct, outcome assessment, and analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe who was blinded and at which stages; refer to the ARRIVE Explanation and Elaboration for good reporting examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items — identify primary and secondary outcome measures and how they were measured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly define outcome measures and measurement timing; examples and further guidance are provided in the E&E document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items — report statistical methods used to analyse the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of statistical tests, assumptions, software, and handling of data; consult ARRIVE E&E for examples and recommended detail level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental animals
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items — provide details about the animals used (species, strain, sex, age, weight, provenance, genetic modification status, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report sufficient information to allow replication and interpretation; see the E&E document for illustrative examples from the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items — describe procedures performed on animals (what was done, how, when, and by whom) in sufficient detail for replication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide step-by-step descriptions, dosages, routes, timings, and equipment where relevant; examples of good reporting are included in the ARRIVE E&E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items — present results for all key outcomes, including measures of precision and effect sizes where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report results transparently including negative/null findings, variability, and any missing data; see the E&E for examples and recommended reporting formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: A Recommended Set item — include an abstract that summarises key elements of the study for clear communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended Set items complement the Essential 10 and provide important context; the ARRIVE E&E gives examples of good abstracts across model organisms and study types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: A Recommended Set item — provide scientific background and rationale for the study, including context and references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the scientific context and justification for the experimental approach; consult the E&E for how much background to include and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: A Recommended Set item — state the specific objectives, hypotheses, or research questions the study addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify primary and secondary objectives and any prespecified hypotheses; examples and guidance are in the Explanation and Elaboration document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.description: A Recommended Set item — report ethical approvals, welfare considerations, and compliance with relevant guidelines or legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include name of approving body, permit numbers, and any steps taken to minimise animal suffering; see ARRIVE E&E for sample wording and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: A Recommended Set item — describe housing conditions and husbandry practices that could influence study outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report details such as cage type, bedding, environmental enrichment, light/dark cycle, temperature, and group housing; consult E&E examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: A Recommended Set item — describe monitoring, care, and any interventions provided to animals during the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail monitoring frequency, humane endpoints, and veterinary care provided; the E&E includes examples of appropriate reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation/ scientific implications
rubrics_metrics.description: A Recommended Set item — interpret results in context, discuss biological significance, limitations, and alternative explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss limitations, sources of bias, and how the findings fit with existing knowledge; see E&E for guidance on balanced interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability/ translation
rubrics_metrics.description: A Recommended Set item — comment on the generalisability of the findings and their potential translational relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address how results may translate across species or to clinical contexts and any caveats; examples provided in the Explanation and Elaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A Recommended Set item — indicate whether the study protocol was preregistered and provide registration details if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report registry name, identifier, and any deviations from the registered protocol; refer to E&E for examples and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access
rubrics_metrics.description: A Recommended Set item — provide information on data availability, including links to datasets or statements on access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State where and how data, code, and materials can be accessed to support reproducibility; the ARRIVE E&E outlines best practices and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests
rubrics_metrics.description: A Recommended Set item — disclose funding sources, conflicts of interest, and any potential competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide transparent statements about financial and non-financial interests and funder roles; see E&E for example disclosures.
